I'm looking for enthusiastic teammates interested in programming, UI/UX design, data analysis, astronomy, research and creative problem-solving.

Beginners are welcome! Curiosity, teamwork and willingness to learn are what matter most.

Let's think beyond Earth and create something extraordinary! 🪐✨
summary:
VIGIL – Autonomous Deep-Space Clinical Decision Support System

VIGIL is an offline-first clinical decision support system designed for astronaut healthcare during long-duration space missions, where communication delays and Deep Space Network blackouts make real-time Earth-based medical support impossible.

Built on NASA ExMC Level IV/V standards and OSDR flight datasets, VIGIL uses a deterministic five-stage engine to establish astronaut-specific baselines using Median and MAD, account for microgravity adaptations, and detect early health deterioration through multi-signal analysis. It monitors 11 vital indicators across six domains, combining slack-based CUSUM tracking and persistence filtering to distinguish genuine health risks from sensor noise and temporary fluctuations.

Its interactive medical cockpit features a 3D anatomical hologram, evidence-linked alerts, guided countermeasures, live timers, respiratory pacing, and supply-aware triage. Closed-loop intervention tracking evaluates treatment effectiveness, while JSON and print-ready telemetry reports support Earth-side medical handovers.

Validated across 600 simulated mission runs, VIGIL achieved 100% event sensitivity while reducing false alarms by approximately 85–90% compared with fixed thresholds and rolling z-scores. Its fully offline PWA architecture uses local IndexedDB storage, enabling autonomous clinical decision support for missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
details:
Project Details – VIGIL: Autonomous Deep-Space Clinical Decision Support System

VIGIL is an autonomous, offline-first medical decision support system designed to protect astronaut health during long-duration deep-space missions, where communication latencies of 12–22 minutes and extended communication blackouts make real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible.

How it works: VIGIL uses a five-stage deterministic mathematical engine. It first establishes personalized pre-flight health baselines (median + MAD), accounts for early in-flight microgravity adaptation offsets, and applies tabular CUSUM change detection to identify persistent physiological drift. It then separates temporary transient spikes and sensor faults from sustained health deterioration and clusters signals across multiple health domains into unified medical alerts. Its interactive cockpit features an anatomical 3D body hologram, evidence-strength indicators, clinical checklists, and interactive procedure tools (including a 5-minute rest timer and breathing pacer). It provides supply-aware triage recommendations based on remaining onboard medical consumables and evaluates countermeasure effectiveness through closed-loop follow-up tracking. Medical telemetry handover packages are generated in store-and-forward JSON and print-ready formats.

Benefits and intended impact: VIGIL reduces operational dependence on Earth-based mission control, identifies subtle physiological deterioration weeks before acute symptoms arise, minimizes false alarms (~89% reduction vs. baseline systems), supports crew medical officers with limited clinical training, and maintains continuous health monitoring through communication blackouts. It aims to make future Lunar and Martian missions safer and medically self-reliant.

Tools and technologies:Three.js, and an offline Progressive Web App (PWA) architecture with local IndexedDB storage. Its mathematical detection engine, frozen clinical guidance library, and zero-backend design eliminate all runtime network and cloud dependencies. Hardware-agnostic: operates locally on standard crew tablets or laptops without requiring specialized compute infrastructure.

Creativity and innovation: Unlike conventional population-threshold alarms, VIGIL uses astronaut-specific baselines, accounts for spaceflight adaptation curves, isolates sensor artifacts from true physiological shifts, and correlates cross-domain signals into unified alerts. It integrates detection, triage, procedure guidance, follow-up evaluation, and flight-surgeon handover reporting into a single cockpit without relying on black-box generative AI or LLMs.

Factors considered: Communication latency, solar conjunction blackouts, microgravity adaptation, individual physiological baselines, wearable sensor dropouts, consumable resource limits, clinical alert fatigue, offline reliability, and the limited clinical training of non-physician crew members.

Evaluation & Validation: Evaluated across 600 simulated crew-mission runs (seeds 1–100 across six operational scenarios), achieving 100% event detection with a median detection delay of 17 days on insidious drifts (0–4 days on acute events) and false alarm rates of 0.62–0.75 per 100 days (compared to ~5.0 for fixed thresholds and ~6.5 for rolling z-scores). Designed for future operational validation in NASA HERA and CHAPEA analog habitat missions.

1. Operational Flight Hardware Requirements

(Target deployment environment on a crewed spacecraft, lunar habitat, or analog mission)

Component Minimum Specification Recommended Spaceflight Target

Device Type Any standard tablet, laptop, or flight-deck console Space-qualified crew tablet (e.g., Apple iPad / Microsoft Surface Pro) or laptop (e.g., ThinkPad / HP ZBook used on the ISS)

Processor (CPU) 64-bit dual-core x86-64 or ARM64 (1.5 GHz+) Quad-core modern mobile processor (Apple Silicon M-series, Intel Core i5+, AMD Ryzen)

RAM 2 GB available RAM 4 GB to 8 GB RAM

Storage 50 MB free disk space 500 MB (app precache bundle is ~2.3 MB; 180 days of multi-indicator daily telemetry occupies < 5 MB in IndexedDB)

Display & Resolution 390 × 844 px (handheld mobile viewport) 1024 × 768 px (tablet) to 1920 × 1080 px (flight deck display); touch-screen enabled with 44px minimum touch targets adhering to NASA-STD-3001 ergonomics

Graphics (GPU) Integrated GPU supporting WebGL 1.0 / 2.0 Any standard integrated GPU for the Three.js 3D anatomical body hologram mesh

Network & Power Zero network connectivity required (fully autonomous air-gapped operation) Battery-powered portable tablet or vehicle bus DC power

2. Operational Software & Runtime Requirements

Architecture: Zero-Backend, Local-First Progressive Web App (PWA).

Supported Browsers:

Chromium-based browsers (Google Chrome 90+, Microsoft Edge 90+, Brave).

WebKit / Safari (iOS / iPadOS 15+, macOS Safari 15+).

Mozilla Firefox 90+.

Browser Capabilities Required:

Service Worker & Cache API: For 100% offline precaching and network-disconnected launch.

IndexedDB: For local, tamper-evident telemetry and journal record persistence.

WebGL: For hardware-accelerated rendering of the 3D anatomical body hologram (three.js).

Runtime Dependencies:

No Cloud / Backend APIs: Zero reliance on remote microservices, external databases, or cloud LLM endpoints.

Router: HashRouter (enables seamless file-system and static hosting without server rewrite rules).

3. Medical Sensor & Peripheral Interfaces

(Input sources for the 11 monitored clinical indicators)

Vigil is input-agnostic. Daily telemetry can be ingested via standard local communication channels (Bluetooth LE / USB) or manual entry:

Cardiovascular: Non-invasive blood pressure (NIBP) oscillometric cuff and continuous photoplethysmography (PPG) / ECG wrist sensor or smart garment (e.g., CSA Bio-Monitor).

Metabolic & Temperature: Infrared tympanic/temporal thermometer and capillary point-of-care blood glucometer.

Sleep & Activity: Tri-axial wrist actigraphy / smart band.

Radiation: Active onboard silicon solid-state dosimeter or area radiation monitor (e.g., ISS PADLES, MSL RAD, or Artemis ESA/NASA active dosimeters).

Consumables: Onboard medical kit inventory status (tracked via built-in supply toggles).

4. Development & Evaluation Environment Requirements

(To build the project, run test suites, or execute the evaluation harness)

Operating System: Windows 10/11, macOS 12+, or modern Linux distribution (Ubuntu 22.04+).

Node.js: Node.js v20.0.0 or higher (v22.x recommended).

Package Manager: npm v10+.

Core Tech Stack:

Language: TypeScript 5.6+ (strict type-checking).

Build Tool: Vite 5.4+.

UI Framework: React 18.3, React Router DOM 6.26.

Styling: Tailwind CSS 3.4 + PostCSS + Autoprefixer.

3D Visualization: Three.js 0.187 (low-poly anatomical GLTF/GLB mesh).

Data Visualization: Recharts 2.12.

Storage Interface: idb 8.0.

Testing & Verification: Vitest 2.1, React Testing Library, fake-indexeddb, and Playwright/Puppeteer for browser QA.
